 Georgia football injury report vs. Ole Miss
 Here's the latest on who's in and who's out for the Bulldogs ahead of Saturday night's game in Oxford.
 Jordan D. Hill 0 The Georgia Bulldogs have another big road game on the docket.
 No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC) will play at No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) in a 7:30 p.m. ET matchup that will be televised by ABC. This will be the third time the teams have played in 10 months after the Bulldogs won last October's matchup 43-35 and the Rebels won January's Sugar Bowl 39-34.
 "[Ole Miss is a] really good football team. Pete [Golding] has done a tremendous job since taking over. Obviously we know the two games with them last year were two really hard-fought battles, hard games, a lot of ebb and flow in both games," Kirby Smart said on Monday. "They've done a tremendous job this year. They've got probably the best quarterback in the country who plays at a high level. He is extremely hard to defend and a great player. A lot of respect for their staff. I know a lot of those guys and the way their team competes and plays."
 Georgia is hoping for more success after taking care of Florida coming off of the Bulldogs' bye week.
 Georgia turned three first-half Florida turnovers into 17 points to set the stage for a 27-8 victory. The turning point for the Bulldogs was the third turnover, when a promising Florida drive ended with a Chris Cole 66-yard fumble return touchdown that helped the Bulldogs take a 24-0 lead.
 The Bulldogs have a handful of banged-up players going into Saturday's game. Here's the latest on the injury front for Georgia.
 Note: Be sure to check back in on this story roughly 1 hour before kickoff. We'll have the latest on who made the trip to Oxford and who is watching the action from home:
 RUNNING BACK CHAUNCEY BOWENS (QUESTIONABLE)
 (Photo: Ethan Greene, 247Sports) 
 Chauncey Bowens is slowly but surely closing in on a return to action.
 Bowens was listed as questionable on the Thursday availability report. He was initially given that status to start the Florida week before being ruled out on Thursday.
 Smart was mum on Bowens' recovery timeline two weeks ago, only saying, "time will tell."
 Bowens played in Georgia's first 5 games this season. He took 35 carries for 124 yards and 6 touchdowns. He also caught 10 passes for 132 yards and 1 touchdown.
 RUNNING BACK DWIGHT PHILLIPS JR. (IN)
 (Photo: Todd Kirkland, Getty) 
 Dwight Phillips Jr. is all set to play an important part in the Georgia ground game.
 Phillips limped off the field in the fourth quarter of Saturday's win over Florida, and the ESPN broadcast mentioned that he had his ankle taped on the sideline. Smart said Phillips was fine on Monday and added that "I think he was more tired than hurt."
 Phillips has stepped up in the Bulldogs backfield this season, especially when Nate Frazier was out with a rib injury. Through eight games, Phillips has taken 55 carries for 415 yards and 2 touchdowns.
 RUNNING BACK DANTE DOWDELL (OUT)
 (Photo: @dante_dowdell) 
 Football is not a top priority for Dante Dowdell  as he tries to recover from injuries suffered in an ATV accident this summer.
 Dowdell shared on social media two weeks ago that he had a 10-hour surgery as his recovery continues. He posted a video on social media five weeks ago that shared that he suffered a punctured lug, broken ribs, broken collarbones, and nerve damage to his right arm. He also received nine staples in his head.
 Dowdell shared a video that showed his slow recovery from the injury. He spent two-and-a-half months in the hospital but has begun rehabbing from his injuries. That includes walking again, working on his motor skills, and building his leg muscles back.
 Smart spoke about Dowdell the day after his video was posted.
 "I think our medical staff, they do a tremendous job. Connor [Norman] and Ryan [Madaleno] have been unbelievable with communication, talking to his family, talking to Shepherd Center in different places," Smart said. "They've been with him every step of the way, along with Coach [Josh] Crawford in the running back room. They got to go over and visit him and see him in Atlanta, and reached out and have talked to him a lot. He's been around the team some, and he knows what his priorities are right now, and that's trying to get healthy."
 Dowdell transferred to Georgia after the 2025 season and was set to use his final year of eligibility with the Bulldogs. He drew positive reviews during spring practice and ended spring in style by taking 6 carries for 61 yards and 1 touchdown at G-Day.
 WIDE RECEIVER ISIAH CANION (IN)
 (Photo: John Adams/Icon Sportswire, Getty) 
 Things are trending in the right direction for Isiah Canion .
 Canion was removed from the availability report on Thursday, indicating he will be available for Saturday's game. He is looking to return to action after missing the past five games due to a leg injury.
 Canion warmed up with the receivers prior to the Florida game while wearing a brace on his right leg. He ultimately did not see the field in the Bulldogs' 27-8 victory.
 Smart hasn't shared much on Canion's status, going back to five weeks ago.
 "I'll refer to the injury report. That's why we do those, right?" Smart said when asked about Canion. "Every other coach says that's what we do them for. People in this room beg for injury reports. You've got one. It comes out every Wednesday. What time? 8:10, so I'm sure y'all are sitting on the edge of your seat waiting to get it. You're dying to get it so you can write another article about it. 
 "You guys are awesome about following those things up. I wait for y'all to write about it so I can find out about the other team. I don't even check it myself. So it'll be out Wednesday at 8:10, maybe a little later."
 Canion suffered his injury during the first quarter at Arkansas. He was evaluated in the injury tent then remained on the sideline for the rest of the action.
 Through three games, the Georgia Tech transfer has 3 receptions for 28 yards as a Bulldog.
 WIDE RECEIVER THOMAS BLACKSHEAR (QUESTIONABLE)
 (Photo: Icon Sportswire, Getty) 
 Thomas Blackshear is also closing in on a return from injury.
 Blackshear was listed as questionable on the first two availability reports of the week. He suffered an apparent injury during Georgia's Week 5 game against Vanderbilt. He re-appeared on the sideline in the second half with his arm in a sling.
 Smart described Blackshear's injury four weeks ago as "an upper-body injury."
 In four games this season, Blackshear has caught 5 passes for 48 yards.
 TIGHT END ELYISS WILLIAMS (QUESTIONABLE)
 (Photo: Dale Zanine, USA TODAY Sports) 
 Elyiss Williams landed on the availability report on Wednesday night. Williams suffered an apparent right ankle injury in the fourth quarter of Saturday's game against Florida. He returned to the game before its conclusion.
 Williams has caught 7 passes for 88 yards and 2 touchdowns this season.
 DEFENSIVE END JOSEPH JONAH-AJONYE (QUESTIONABLE)
 (Photo: CFP, Getty) 
 Georgia may be down a defensive end on Saturday. Joseph Jonah-Ajonye was listed as questionable on the Thursday availability report. It is unclear what injury Jonah-Ajonye is dealing with at this time.
 Jonah-Ajonye has appeared in all eight games for the Bulldogs this season. His biggest moment came in Week 6, when he sacked Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell and forced a fumble on the Crimson Tide's first drive. 
 Jonah-Ajonye has recorded 11 tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 1 sack, and 1 forced fumble this season.
 OUTSIDE LINEBACKER AMARIS WILLIAMS (OUT)
 (Photo: Benjamin Wolk, 247Sports) 
 The major injury development for Georgia in the spring concerned Amaris Williams . The Auburn transfer hurt his knee, and there is concern it may cost him the entire 2026 season .
 Williams was one of eight players that Georgia added from the transfer portal this offseason. A former 5-star recruit from Clinton, North Carolina, Williams flashed his potential during two seasons at Auburn. 
 Smart gave the latest on Williams' recovery last week.
 "[He's] doing great. He's working hard," Smart said. "Day to day, he comes out with us and is able to get some parts of a practice like flex and does some things with us to stay part of the group. But he's not in any shape to play or anything right now." 
 Smart said he didn't know if Williams would be able to play this season.
 Williams is coming off a 2025 season during which he played in 11 games and recorded 14 tackles, 6 tackles for loss, and 2 sacks. His workload increased after a freshman season in which he played in 10 games and logged 6 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, and 0.5 sacks.
 OUTSIDE LINEBACKER DARREN IKINNAGBON (OUT)
 (Photo: Benjamin Wolk, 247Sports) 
 Darren Ikinnagbon remains out for Georgia.
 Ikinnagbon was spotted with a boot on his right foot during pre-game warm-ups for the Oklahoma game. Smart declined to give insight on Ikinnagbon's situation, again referring to the availability report. Ikinnagbon has not been listed on the report this season.
 Ikinnagbon played against Tennessee State and Western Kentucky to start the season. He has 4 total tackles but did not make the trip to Arkansas.
 Ikinnagbon played in five games last season. He recorded 2 tackles.
 INSIDE LINEBACKER AJ KRUAH (QUESTIONABLE)
 (Photo: Ethan Greene, 247Sports) 
 Linebacker AJ Kruah is working through injury this week. He was listed as questionable on the Thursday availability report.
 Kruah has been a reserve linebacker as a sophomore, but he's made some big plays on special teams. His biggest to date was forcing a fumble on the opening kickoff of the Bulldogs' game against Western Kentucky in Week 2.
 In eight games this season, Kruah has 13 tackles, 1 tackle for loss, and 1 forced fumble.
 CORNERBACK ELLIS ROBINSON IV (IN)
 (Photo: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire, Getty) 
 Georgia avoided a real injury concern in Ellis Robinson IV . Robinson tweaked his knee during the first half of the Florida game and ultimately did not return to the action.
 Smart said after the game that Robinson's knee tightened up on him but that Smart didn't think there was anything structurally wrong. Smart gave a positive report on Robinson on Monday, saying, "He looks good. Hopefully he'll be good to go."
 Robinson has been a lock-down corner this season. Through eight games, he has 15 tackles, 5 pass break-ups, and 2 interceptions.
 SAFETY TYRIQ GREEN (QUESTIONABLE)
 (Photo: Tony Walsh/UGAAA) 
 Tyriq Green continues to work his way back from an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. The freshman was listed as questionable on the Thursday availability report. 
 Green injured his ankle late in the fourth quarter of Saturday's game against Western Kentucky. It was a disappointing close to a big day for the freshman, who recovered a fumble in the end zone for a touchdown and also had a 91-yard kick return touchdown. 
 Green's special teams score marked the first time that Georgia had a kick return touchdown since Terry Godwin in 2016.
 "T-Green, we're finding more and more out on," Smart said to open Arkansas week. "We'll see what the deal is with him as the week goes on if he's able to play or not."
 Green was spotted on campus last week no longer wearing a boot on his injured foot.
